poor care for years upon years.

My Nana had been told some time ago, under both Dr. Gudi and Mrs. Gudi, that she had asthma. This came after she reported tightness in her chest, shortness of breath and pain in her arms. She was never invited for tests, only prescribed steroid inhalers.

It was a hospital nurse who recognised that she had heart failure. Thankfully, my Nana is still alive.

She has told me that the regular staff tend to be very dismissive and condescending towards her, which appears to be a theme when skimming other reviews. I was unfortunate to experience that first-hand when Nana had a telephone appointment earlier today.

Since she is somewhat hard of hearing I often attend appointments with her, telephone or otherwise. The nurse asked my Nana to move elsewhere so that there wasn't an "echo" because she could hear me. This wasn't requested out of respect for privacy, nor did she address me despite being clearly able to hear me. My Nana didn't move but I certainly kept my mouth shut and listened to what was being said. Neither of us appreciated the way that the nurse spoke to her.

The nurse also told us that my Nana hasn't been in receipt of a cholesterol blood test since February 2024. She's had her cholesterol levels tested in hospital during PCI procedures and subsequent treatment with medication, as far as we've been made aware. Her cholesterol is being treated, if only her notes would be examined. The consultants weren't about to allow her to leave hospital without this treatment in place.

Time and time again, staff at this surgery have taken a stance of "I've studied and qualified, and therefore know your body better than you do". This is never a supportive stance for any clinician to be taking in any area of healthcare. If anything is contested, nobody seems to bat an eyelash.

We'll be transferring her care elsewhere following the holiday period. Personally, I'm amazed that this practice is still
